plain: The intent to do harm to another

webster.text: Extreme enmity of heart, or malevolence; a disposition to injure others without cause, from mere personal gratification or from a spirit of revenge; unprovoked malignity or spite.

more.text: To regard with extreme ill will.

example.quote: Their menial servants may enter, may break locks, bars, and everything in their way; and whether they break through malice or revenge, no man, no court can inquire.
example.cite: James Otis, Argument Against Writs of Assistance, 1761
